subject: Acme: Post-call recap — concurrency & Redwood rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme: Post-call recap — concurrency & Redwood rate limits

Thanks for the time this morning, Alex — good conversation. Recap below and next steps so we have alignment on performance targets and the capacity request.

Call summary (short):
- Traffic profile: product recommendations service, primarily streaming completions for incremental user-facing suggestions.
- Current traffic today: ~500 concurrent streaming sessions during normal peaks, 1.2k during flash events.
- Target for launch: support sustained 800 concurrent streaming sessions with headroom to 2.5k during 10-minute spikes.
- Latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end token latency target <= 200ms for non-streamed completions; streaming initial-token latency <= 120ms.
- Throughput: sustained ~120 req/s across region, burst up to 1.5k req/s for short periods.
- Connection behavior: clients will use HTTP keep-alive and connection pooling; average session holds an open streaming connection ~45s.

Ask we discussed: Acme is requesting an increase to Redwood's hosted concurrency quota to allow 2,500 parallel requests (across their org), plus an elevated token-rate quota to cover burst windows. They also asked about connection limits per IP and recommended pooling patterns.

Attachments: I attached the ACME_Rate_Limits_Request.xlsx you shared and our initial Redwood_SLO_Proposal_v2.pdf. Please confirm the numbers below are correct so I can get internal approval for the quota bump and confirm any dedicated-capacity recommendation.

Proposed next steps:
1) Alex to confirm peak concurrency and burst duration details (answered in the sheet).
2) We (Redwood) will validate feasibility of a 2.5k concurrency quota on hosted plan vs recommending Dedicated capacity + reserved concurrency.
3) If hosted quota is required, Redwood will start an internal review with infra + rate-limits (ETA 48 business hours) and come back with recommended controls (per-route limits, token caps, connection pool guidance).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: ACME_Rate_Limits_Request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB); Redwood_SLO_Proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call recap — concurrency & Redwood rate limits

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 1.2k flash events are typically 6–12 minutes (we see a very spiky traffic pattern during vendor promos).
- Sustained baseline for Q1 is likely 700–850 concurrent streaming sessions (we'll budget for 800).
- Connection pooling: our SDK will reuse connections from a small set of EC2 instances (we expect ~60 client IPs / origin). Let me know if you need IP ranges or anything else for testing.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood raise the hosted concurrency quota to 2,500 while we validate in prod for 4 weeks? If not possible, what's the recommended dedicated configuration and estimated cost delta?
2) Can we get a temporary elevation to token-rate limits to handle the promo bursts (we estimate ~20M tokens over a 12-minute flash window at peak)?

I'll upload a filled copy of your sheet with peak-duration details — attaching now.

—Alex

Attachments: ACME_Rate_Limits_Request_filled.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 14:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call recap — concurrency & Redwood rate limits

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alex — got the filled sheet. Two notes after syncing with infra (Dylan included):

1) Hosted vs Dedicated:
   - Hosted: we can often accommodate higher concurrency by adjusting per-customer buckets and global capacity, but persistent 2.5k parallel streaming sessions with 45s average session time and 1.5k req/s bursts puts pressure on multi-tenant pools. We can start with a hosted quota bump for a limited pilot (4 weeks) while we monitor impact; this would be an internal-exception flow and requires a short review from infra (expected approval window 48–72 hours once we submit).
   - Dedicated: recommended if you need sustained 2.5k+ concurrency with guaranteed latency SLOs—gives reserved GPUs and predictable throughput. We can provide a cost delta after we map the expected sustained qps and token consumption.

2) Temporary token-rate elevation for promo windows:
   - Short-term option: temporary elevation for planned promo windows (Doc-level approval + signed MPA). We'll need the exact window timings and token estimate per window.
   - Controls we propose: per-route burst caps, global token bucket for promo sessions, and an automatic fallback to a slightly smaller-model variant if utilization hits >85% of capacity.

3) Connection pooling guidance:
   - Keep-alive + HTTP/2 (preferred) to keep concurrent connection counts low. With ~60 origin IPs, we recommend limiting simultaneous TCP connections per IP to 50 and using long-lived streams.

Next steps (internal routing): Dylan, can you start the hosted-quota exception ticket and attach the filled ACME sheet + our SLO proposal? Laura, please prep a rough Dedicated sizing note (gpus, sustained qps) we can share with Alex if hosted exception is denied.

Alex — once infra confirms the hosted exception path, we'll share the exact quota numbers and the temporary token-rate window process.

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (template, 12KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call recap — concurrency & Redwood rate limits

Looping in infra. Marissa — I opened ticket INFRA-QUOTA-7729 for the hosted exception and attached the ACME sheet + Redwood_SLO_Proposal_v2.pdf. Summary of the infra assessment so far:

- Preliminary: Hosted pilot OK for a time-limited 4-week elevation to 2,500 parallel requests, subject to NOC monitoring and automated throttles. We'll enforce per-route burst caps and a global token ceiling.
- We will provision an alerting rule at 85% capacity and an automatic fallback policy (model variant degrade) at 92%.
- For sustained needs >2.5k, recommend Dedicated configuration: 4x A100-equivalent reserved nodes (approx estimate) — Laura will follow with a sizing/cost breakout.

Action items captured:
- INFRA-QUOTA-7729: hosted exception review (owner: infra ops, ETA 48–72h).
- LAURA: Dedicated sizing + preliminary quote (2 business days).
- MARISSA/ALEX: sign mutual_action_plan.xlsx to authorize temporary token-rate windows and scheduled promo dates.

Alex — if you can confirm the 12-minute promo windows and the token estimate (20M tokens) in the signed MAP, we can kick off the temporary elevation once INFRA-QUOTA-7729 is approved.

Thanks — Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Technical Program Manager, Inference Operations
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: Redwood_SLO_Proposal_v2.pdf (attached in ticket)
